title: WASP: Workload-Aware Self-Replicating Page-Tables for NUMA Servers
problem: Page-table self-replication (PTSR) reduces NUMA effects for large-memory workloads but may improve or hurt performance depending on workload characteristics and co-located applications. Current PTSR systems can only be manually enabled or disabled by users.
motivation: Large-memory workloads on NUMA servers suffer from page-table-caused NUMA effects, and users need automatic mechanisms to determine when PTSR is beneficial.
method: WASP automatically profiles how an application accesses memory and monitors interference from other running applications to decide whether to enable page-table self-replication—storing copies of the memory-mapping table across processor cores instead of keeping just one. Based on these observations, it turns PTSR on when it improves performance and off when it creates overhead. This eliminates the need for users to manually configure PTSR.
key_novelty: WASP automatically decides whether to enable page-table self-replication by observing application memory access and interference from co-running applications, instead of requiring manual configuration.
contributions: Workload-aware mechanism for automatic PTSR enablement/disablement based on application characteristics
Detection algorithm to identify when PTSR improves versus hurts performance
System design integrating workload profiling with autonomous PTSR policy
Evaluation demonstrating performance improvements over manual PTSR configuration

metrics.speedup: improvement over baseline and manual PTSR

primary_theme: automatic NUMA optimization via workload-aware page-table replication
